𝟭𝟰.𝟯𝟱 𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘆 𝗶𝘀 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗷𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗮 𝘂𝘀𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝘀𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘀𝘁𝗶𝗰.

It is what happens when an AI platform stops behaving like a showroom for models and starts behaving like infrastructure.

On August 4, https://t.co/YpD1NBsBFD reported that after integrating Qwen3.8-Max, daily compute throughput for the model surpassed 14.35 billion tokens—a recent high for the ecosystem.

Think about what 14.35 billion tokens actually means.

Not one impressive prompt.

Not one developer testing a new model.

Millions of fragments of work moving through the same access layer:

Code being inspected.

Documents being analysed.

Images being understood.

Agents planning their next action.

Repositories being searched.

Research being synthesised.

Applications making API calls while their users never even see the model underneath.

That is the part of the AI economy people often miss.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝗱𝗲𝗹 𝗶𝘀 𝗼𝗻𝗹𝘆 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝗹𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿.

Someone still has to make the model reachable.

Bill the request.

Measure the tokens.

Handle different providers.

Expose a usable API.

Give developers visibility into consumption.

Allow another model to take over when the workload changes.

And keep doing this when demand suddenly becomes enormous.

https://t.co/YpD1NBsBFD is positioning itself around that layer.

Its current catalogue already spans model families from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, xAI, https://t.co/wARwt37KQR, Moonshot and Qwen rather than forcing every developer into one intelligence provider.

Now imagine an AI company processing 100,000 tasks.

Task 1 is simple extraction.

Using the most expensive reasoning model would waste money.

Task 2 requires analysis across an enormous codebase.

A lightweight model may fail.

Task 3 contains images and text.

Task 4 is an agent running a long sequence of tool calls.

Task 5 needs a fast answer because a human is waiting.

The intelligent decision is not:

“Which model is the best?”

There is no universally best model.

The useful question is:

Which model gives this particular workload the right combination of capability, speed and cost?

This is why https://t.co/YpD1NBsBFD’s expanding model layer matters.

Qwen3.8-Max itself illustrates the direction.

https://t.co/YpD1NBsBFD documents it with a Mixture-of-Experts architecture, multimodal text/image/video input and long-context capabilities intended for coding, professional knowledge work and agentic workloads.

But tomorrow the strongest model for another job may come from somewhere else.

That should not require the developer to rebuild the entire product.

The application should remain.

The workflow should remain.

The API relationship should remain manageable.

The intelligence underneath should be replaceable.

That becomes even more important for AI agents.

A serious agent may perform twenty different cognitive jobs during one objective.

Classification.

Search.

Planning.

Coding.

Vision.

Reasoning.

Summarisation.

Verification.

Why should all twenty automatically go through the same model?

https://t.co/YpD1NBsBFD’s Auto Mode already moves toward request-level model selection, while its billing records charge according to the model actually used, tokens consumed and applicable tool usage rather than pretending “Auto” is one mysterious model.

This creates something much more interesting than another AI chat interface.

𝗜𝘁 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗹𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲.

Models compete on:

Capability.

Latency.

Context.

Multimodality.

Reasoning depth.

And cost.

Developers consume whichever intelligence fits the workload.

Users pay for actual usage.

Agents can eventually treat models as interchangeable computational resources rather than personalities they are permanently married to.

And that is why the 14.35 billion-token day matters.

The number is not impressive because tokens are inherently valuable.

It is impressive because every token represents demand passing through an abstraction layer connecting users, applications and different forms of machine intelligence.

The future AI platform may not win by building the one model that defeats every other model.

It may win by becoming the place where every useful model can compete to perform the next job.

That is the infrastructure game https://t.co/YpD1NBsBFD is beginning to play.

HON. NOAH AHMED — EMPOWERING THE GEN Z GENERATION

Hon. Noah Ahmed’s proposed vision for young people is built on one fundamental principle: young people should not only be the leaders of tomorrow—they should have meaningful opportunities to contribute today.

His youth empowerment agenda would focus on turning the energy, creativity and innovation of Gen Z into skills, businesses, employment and sustainable livelihoods across Taraba State.

Under this proposed vision, youth development would include:

💡 TECHNOLOGY & DIGITAL SKILLS
Create opportunities for young people to learn AI, cybersecurity, software development, digital marketing, graphics, content creation and other emerging technologies.

🚀 STARTUP & BUSINESS SPONSORSHIP
Support promising youth-owned businesses through transparent grants, equipment, mentorship and access to business development programmes—not just one-time handouts.

🎓 EDUCATION & SCHOLARSHIPS
Expand opportunities for scholarships, vocational training, professional certifications and technical education so that financial hardship does not prevent talented young people from developing their potential.

🎨 CREATIVE INDUSTRY SUPPORT
Provide structured support for musicians, filmmakers, photographers, designers, writers, fashion entrepreneurs and other creatives through training, sponsorship and platforms for showcasing their work.

⚽ SPORTS DEVELOPMENT
Invest in grassroots sports by supporting young athletes, coaches and sporting programmes, while creating pathways for talented youths to compete at higher levels.

💼 JOBS, INTERNSHIPS & ENTREPRENEURSHIP
Build partnerships with private businesses and institutions to create internships, apprenticeships and employment opportunities while helping young entrepreneurs develop sustainable enterprises.

🏢 YOUTH INNOVATION CENTRES
Develop spaces where young people can access training, internet connectivity, mentorship, technology and collaborative opportunities.

A NEW APPROACH TO YOUTH SPONSORSHIP

The goal should be to move from “giving young people something” to “giving young people the tools to build something.”

Every sponsorship programme should be transparent, merit-based and accessible to young people across communities and local government areas.

HON. NOAH AHMED’S MESSAGE TO THE GEN Z GENERATION:

> “Your ideas matter. Your talent matters. Your future matters. Government should create an environment where a young person with an idea, skill or dream has a genuine opportunity to turn that potential into reality.”

Empower the youth. Invest in talent. Sponsor innovation. Create opportunity. Build a stronger Taraba.

Ultra-realistic luxury fashion editorial portrait of a handsome young man with thick, voluminous dark brown hair styled in a refined textured quiff, neatly faded sides, and a full, sharply groomed beard. He is shown in a sophisticated three-quarter close-up profile, looking downward with a calm, confident expression. He wears classic black rectangular sunglasses with subtle premium detailing, a textured black waffle-knit cardigan worn slightly open at the chest, and a minimalist luxury wristwatch with a black dial, slim silver case, and black leather strap.

His right hand naturally adjusts the collar of the cardigan, bringing attention to the watch and refined styling. Warm natural skin tones, realistic beard and individual hair strands, detailed skin texture, subtle facial pores, elegant masculine aesthetic. Clean turquoise-blue studio background with a softly blurred beige foreground, creating a premium contemporary contrast. Soft directional daylight from the upper left, gentle highlights along the face and hair, subtle shadows, cinematic depth of field, shallow background blur, sophisticated luxury campaign photography, premium menswear advertisement, understated elegance, photorealistic, high-end editorial photography, 85mm portrait lens, f/1.8, natural bokeh, crisp subject separation, realistic proportions, 8K detail, vertical composition, no text, no watermark.

Negative prompt: cartoon, CGI, plastic skin, over-smoothed face, distorted hands, extra fingers, malformed watch, asymmetrical sunglasses, exaggerated muscles, oversaturated colors, artificial lighting, blurry face, low detail, duplicate accessories, warped anatomy.

Native ads are one of the hardest ones to make actually work.

The image part is easy, just create a batch of 20 variants. Done. But the hard part is the storytelling and taking a reader from unaware to fully aware.

My ideal set up for the copy is:

1. Hook -> STOP the scroll + create curiosity
2. Problem -> Make them recognize themselves
3. Failed solutions -> WHY what they tried didn't work
4. Mechanism -> Explain what's ACTUALLY causing the problem
5. Solution -> Introduce your product naturally
6. Proof -> Reviews / authority / results
7. Offer -> Give them a reason to take action

The magic happens in the storytelling. Make it personal so someone from your ICP can literally think: “this is me.”

Talking in the same language as your ICP makes the storytelling actually stick (so research the keywords/language your audience uses in FB groups, Reddit etc). 

We often see that a PDP works best in these cases when the copy is good. Bc the long-form primary text basically works as your prelander.
